<skill_content name="structurizr-validate-loop">
# Skill: structurizr-validate-loop

# Structurizr Validate Loop

You are checking Structurizr DSL with the Structurizr MCP server. Your
host prefixes the MCP tool names (for example `structurizr_validate`;
the in-harness server name is `structurizr`), so refer to the tools by
their own names — the `parse`, `validate`, and `inspect` tools of the
Structurizr MCP server — and call whichever prefixed variant your host
exposes.

## The mandatory loop

Every DSL result runs through this loop before it is returned:

1. **Parse.** Run the `parse` tool on the DSL text. Fix every error it
   reports and parse again.
2. **Validate until OK.** Run the `validate` tool. If it reports
   errors, fix them and re-run. Keep going until `validate` answers
   `OK` — do not move on, and do not report the model as done, before
   it does.
3. **Inspect.** Run the `inspect` tool on the validated text.
4. **Triage EVERY finding** into exactly one of the three labels:
   - **fix** — correct the DSL. Any edit after the final validate
     requires re-validating, so the fixed text re-enters the loop at
     step 2.
   - **expected under the MCP limits** — the finding is caused by a
     limit of the MCP (below), not by the model. Do not chase it.
   - **reported in the final answer** — a genuine recommendation that
     is not fixed now; state it in the final answer.

   A finding that cannot be cleared under the MCP never blocks the
   result.
5. **Return the exact text that last got `OK` from `validate`.** Never
   return text that was never validated to `OK`, and never return text
   that changed after the final validate: if anything is edited after
   the final validate, re-run `validate` (and `inspect` on the new
   text) before returning.

A DSL result that was only parsed, and not validated to `OK`, is NOT a
pass — a parsed-only or reported-only result is not a pass. This is the
same rule as the repo's own PlantUML validation chain (ADR
7a626b12-b189-4561-a51d-ffb2e9e133b4): a structure-only check is not a
pass.

## What the two tools answer

`validate` answers "will this parse into a workspace?" — it is
blocking, and its `OK` is the only green light this skill has.
`inspect` answers "does this follow C4 and Structurizr
recommendations?" — its findings are recommendations, never a failed
validate. See `references/validate-vs-inspect.md` for the side-by-side
table and the common findings with their triage.

## The MCP limits

The Structurizr MCP tools have hard limits; state them in the final
answer whenever they affect the result:

- **DSL text only, single file.** The tools work on the workspace's
  DSL text given as one input; there is no multi-file workspace.
- **`!include`, `!docs`, and `!adrs` are refused.** A DSL that uses any
  of them gets a refusal that reads like "feature … is not enabled" —
  the MCP sandbox does not enable those importers. Do not use them,
  and never "fix" a missing-documentation or missing-decisions finding
  by adding `!docs`/`!adrs`: triage that finding as expected under the
  MCP limits and report it as expected in the final answer.
- **No image rendering.** The MCP cannot produce image files (PNG/SVG).
  Its export tools emit diagram source only — PlantUML, C4-PlantUML,
  or Mermaid text. If images are requested, say so.

## When the MCP is absent

If the Structurizr MCP tools are not available in the host, validation
is not possible. State that in the final answer and never describe a
DSL result as validated — a result the tools could not check is
unvalidated, no matter how well it looks.

## Gotchas that surface in the loop

`references/dsl-gotchas.md` collects the DSL rules whose violations the
loop most often meets: declaration order (elements before the
relationships that use them), quoting, a description and a technology
on every relationship, and flat, model-wide-unique identifiers.

16: | Message | Cause | Fix |
17: |---|---|---|

9: The DSL is parsed top to bottom. An element must be declared before any
10: relationship that references it. A forward reference fails with
11: `The destination element "x" does not exist` — the same error as a
12: typo, so check the identifier first, then the order. Declare all

30:   "Reads orders from", "Publishes events to". Avoid "Uses" and "Calls".
31: - The technology answers "what would I edit or configure?":
32:   "Express Router", "TypeORM", "Kafka topic orders.v1", "PostgreSQL

I've loaded the skill. Key constraint to keep in mind: the Structurizr MCP tool only accepts **a single file of DSL text**, and it **rejects `!include`/`!docs`**. So my plan is as follows:

1. Set up a multi-file workspace in `/work` (root `workspace.dsl` + `!include`d model/view/config files + a `!docs` folder containing Markdown pages).
2. Generate an inlined single-file copy (in `/tmp/opencode`) that exactly matches the multi-file workspace.
3. Run the parse → validate → inspect loop against that inlined copy, and triage all findings.

Creating the workspace files:

input.content:
!docs "docs"

workspace "Web Shop" "A reference multi-file Structurizr workspace for the Web Shop team" {
    !include "model/persons.dsl"
    !include "model/systems.dsl"
    !include "model/components.dsl"
    !include "model/relationships.dsl"
    !include "views/views.dsl"
    !include "config/config.dsl"
}

model {
    customer -> storefront "Browses products and places orders" "HTTPS"
    storefront -> orderApi "Submits orders and reads order status" "HTTPS/JSON"
    orderApi -> orderDb "Persists and queries orders" "JDBC/SQL"
    orderApi -> paymentGateway "Charges the customer's card" "HTTPS/JSON"
    orderController -> orderService "Delegates order processing" "In-process call"
    orderService -> orderRepository "Loads and saves order data" "In-process call"
}

# Web Shop

The Web Shop is an online store. Customers browse the product catalogue
in the **Web Storefront** (a React single-page application) and place
orders through the **Order API** (Node.js / Express).

## Key properties

- Orders are persisted in the **Order Database** (PostgreSQL 16).
- Card payments are delegated to the external **Payment Gateway**.
- The Order API is the only container that talks to the database and
  to the payment gateway; the storefront never does.

## Diagrams

| View | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Context | The customer, the Web Shop, and the Payment Gateway |
| Containers | The storefront, the Order API, and the Order Database |
| Order API Components | The controller, service, and repository inside the Order API |

input.content:
# Architecture Decisions

This page records the decisions behind the Web Shop model. It is
associated with the workspace through the `!docs` directive in
`workspace.dsl`.

## D-001: The storefront talks only to the Order API

The Web Storefront is a static single-page application. It sends order
requests to the Order API over HTTPS/JSON and never connects to the
Order Database or the Payment Gateway directly.

**Consequences**

- The database schema and the payment integration can change without
  touching the storefront.
- All order traffic is observable in one place (the Order API).

## D-002: Components are modelled only for the Order API

The Order API is the only container with internal structure in this
workspace. Its controller, service, and repository are modelled as
components; the storefront and the database are kept at container
level.

**Consequences**

- The component diagram stays small and readable.
- If the storefront grows internal structure, add a second component
  view rather than expanding this one.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path('/work/workspace.dsl')
out = []
for line in root.read_text().splitlines():
    m = re.match(r'\s*!include\s+"([^"]+)"', line)
    if m:
        out.append(pathlib.Path('/work', m.group(1)).read_text().rstrip())
        continue
    if re.match(r'\s*!docs\b', line):
        continue
    out.append(line)
pathlib.Path('/tmp/opencode/workspace.inlined.dsl').write_text('\n'.join(out) + '\n')
print('written')
EOF

awk '
  /^[[:space:]]*!include[[:space:]]+"/ {
    line = $0
    sub(/^[[:space:]]*!include[[:space:]]*"/, "", line)
    sub(/".*$/, "", line)
    while ((getline l < ("/work/" line)) > 0) print l
    close("/work/" line)
    next
  }
  /^[[:space:]]*!docs/ { next }
  { print }
' /work/workspace.dsl > /tmp/opencode/workspace.inlined.dsl
echo "--- inlined file ---"
cat /tmp/opencode/workspace.inlined.dsl

part.text:
Done. The multi-file workspace is set up in `/work` and checked through the full parse → validate → inspect loop.

## What was set up

```
/work
├── workspace.dsl              # root: !docs "docs" + workspace block with !include
├── model/
│   ├── persons.dsl            # customer (person)
│   ├── systems.dsl            # webshop (3 containers) + paymentGateway; includes components.dsl inside the Order API container
│   ├── components.dsl         # controller / service / repository
│   └── relationships.dsl      # all 6 relationships (declared after every element)
├── views/views.dsl            # Context, Containers, OrderApiComponents views
├── config/config.dsl          # scope softwaresystem
└── docs/                      # !docs folder
    ├── overview.md
    └── decisions.md
```

The sample model is a small "Web Shop" system (storefront → order API → database, plus an external payment gateway) so the workspace is a working reference, not an empty skeleton.

## How it was checked

The Structurizr MCP tools take **DSL text as a single file and refuse `!include`/`!docs`** (the sandbox doesn't enable those importers), so I generated an inlined single-file copy (`/tmp/workspace.inlined.dsl`) that is byte-for-byte the multi-file workspace with the includes expanded, and ran the loop on that:

1. **parse** — passed (after two fixes the loop surfaced, see below)
2. **validate** — **OK**
3. **inspect** — 2 findings, both triaged as **expected under the MCP limits**:
   - *"Web Shop" has containers, but is missing documentation* — the docs exist via `!docs "docs"` in the real workspace; the MCP can't see them because it refuses `!docs`. Not fixable in the inlined text, and per convention I did not chase it.
   - *"Web Shop" has containers, but is missing decisions* — same cause: decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions.md`, but the MCP refuses `!adrs`/`!docs`.

No other findings: every element has a description, every relationship has a description and a technology, all views have explicit identifier keys, and the workspace scope is set.

## Fixes the loop forced (worth knowing for the team convention)

- **One `model` block per workspace.** The parser rejects multiple `model { }` blocks, so the `!include` directives live *inside* the single `model`/`views`/`configuration` blocks in `workspace.dsl`, and the included files contain bare statements (no block wrappers).
- **Components must be declared inside their container's block** — you can't reopen an element later with `orderApi { ... }`. That's why `model/components.dsl` is included from inside the `orderApi` container declaration in `model/systems.dsl`.
- **View keys are identifiers** (`a-zA-Z0-9_-` only) — the component view key is `OrderApiComponents`, not `"Order API Components"`.

One more MCP limit to be aware of: it can't render images (PNG/SVG) — its export tools emit diagram source only (PlantUML / C4-PlantUML / Mermaid), so if the team wants rendered diagrams they'll need the regular Structurizr tooling for that.
